title: MiTiSegmenter: Software for high throughput segmentation and meshing of microCT data in microtiter plate arrays
author: Connah, Michael, et al.

steps.title: Acquire microCT data
steps.instruction: Scan the stacked specimens on a Nikon XTEK XTH 225 kV cabinet scanner (Nikon Metrology, Tring) equipped with a 3000 × 3000‑pixel detector and tungsten target using the following settings: 48 µm voxel resolution, 120 kV voltage, 110 µA current, 0.1 mm copper filter, and 5013 projections. Reconstruct the raw projection data into a 3‑D volume with Nikon’s XCT software and export the result as a 32‑bit .vol file (~80 GB). Optionally down‑sample the dataset to 95 µm (8‑bit) to obtain a ~670 MB file for sharing.

steps.title: Load dataset into MiTiSegmenter
steps.instruction: On a PC with Intel i7‑7700 (3.60 GHz), 64 GB DDR4 RAM, and GTX 1080 Ti (11 GB), load the 8‑bit dataset (3191 × 3191 × 1869 voxels). Loading should take ~4 minutes. Down‑sample the volume by a factor of 4 before processing.

substeps.instruction: Open MiTiSegmenter and import the .vol (or TIFF) file.
Apply a greyscale threshold of 52 to remove background noise.
Run image blobbing to eliminate any remaining mount voxels that are smaller than the smallest sample.
Assign the labelling grid that matches the microtiter‑plate layout.

steps.title: Export processed data
steps.instruction: Export three TIFF stacks (raw, mask, processed) and the corresponding .ply surface model for each specimen; export time averages 40 seconds per specimen.

steps.title: Optional manual segmentation in InVesalius
steps.instruction: For comparison, import the same dataset into InVesalius and perform a manual segmentation using the steps below.

substeps.instruction: Apply a global greyscale threshold of 50 (determined by eye) to separate bone from air.
Select the specimen of interest with the ‘select parts’ tool and move it to a new mask.
Use the threshold paintbrush tool (greyscale range 40‑255) slice‑by‑slice to capture additional regions of slightly lower density.
Create a 3‑D surface model with the ‘binary’ function, ensuring no smoothing is applied.
Export the surface model as a .ply file.

steps.title: Compare meshes in CloudCompare
steps.instruction: Align the MiTiSegmenter and InVesalius meshes using Iterative Closest Point in CloudCompare, then calculate mesh distances. Report the mean inter‑mesh distance (7.7 µm) and standard deviation (120 µm) relative to the scan resolution of 48 µm. Note that one parhypurapophysis (~30 mm maximum dimension) was not captured by the global threshold of MiTiSegmenter but was resolved manually.
